entries.title: Robotics
entries.final_prompt:
Create a premium collectible hobby illustration. The artwork should feel cinematic, aspirational, emotionally warm, commercially polished, and immediately readable on a small mobile card. Use a strong focal subject, crisp subject separation, rich but controlled colour, atmospheric depth, premium lighting, and clear visual storytelling. Sell the emotional fantasy of doing the hobby rather than merely depicting an object. Aim for the feel of a miniature lifestyle hero illustration inside one coherent collectible-art universe, not a poster, advertisement, editorial cover, card face, or designed page. Keep edges and subject readability cleaner than soft editorial painting. No text, no logo, no typography, no card border, no rarity badge, no watermark, no UI.

The hobby or interest name is semantic context only and must never appear visually. Never render the hobby name, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, body copy, text box, lower-third, or typography-like decoration. Do not reserve blank layout space for text and do not turn the composition into a poster, advertisement, magazine cover, card face, or editorial page. Any incidental real-world surface that could carry writing must be blank, abstract, cropped away, turned away, or too indistinct to read.

Treat every monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, camera display, dashboard, terminal, and digital panel as a physical prop rather than a semantic canvas. Prefer no visible screen surface at all. Recognition must come from the person, physical tool, device, prototype, controller, camera, microphone, hardware, object, or real-world action. If a screen is genuinely unavoidable, show only its back, edge, steep oblique angle, dark/blank surface, or a heavily defocused field of broad colour/image shapes; keep it small and secondary. Never present a front-facing readable display, interface, editing timeline, waveform panel, code window, terminal, menu, chat, dashboard, spreadsheet, labels, controls, icons, or text-like UI structure.

Use this overall composition approach: Show a person actively building, testing, configuring, measuring, or creating with technology through clear physical interaction with hardware, a prototype, sensor, robot, circuit, device, camera, instrument, controller, or material object. The physical process must carry the concept. Prefer no visible screen surface. If a display is unavoidable, show only its back/edge or a small steeply-angled dark/blank/defocused surface that cannot carry interface semantics. Medium layered workstation or maker-bench view centered on hands, face, hardware, prototype, and physical cause-and-effect; keep any display edge small, peripheral, and non-readable. The emotional feeling should be curiosity, creation, experimentation, future. Make the hobby immediately recognizable through Subfield-specific hardware, physical process, input device, prototype, experiment, indicator lights, mechanical response, or real-world output should identify the technology without relying on a screen..

Compose the specific scene this way: The person actively manipulates hardware, controls, a prototype, stylus-on-blank-surface, camera, sensor, device, robot, circuit, or other concrete technology input. Use physical indicators, movement, materials, lights, or mechanical response instead of a visible interface. No front-facing screen. Three-quarter medium workstation or maker-bench view emphasizing hands, physical tools, and the object being changed. Use Controlled modern light with a clear face/hands/tool focal hierarchy and minimal display glow..

Use this colour and material direction: cool modern base with controlled warm human accents. avoid generic cyberpunk, show purposeful interaction.

Depict this activity: A person actively building, configuring, experimenting with, or creating through Robotics, with the subfield-specific interaction clearly visible

Place it in this believable setting: A modern but believable workspace, lab, maker bench, or home setup appropriate to Robotics

The emotional tone should feel curiosity, creation, problem-solving, future-facing energy.

Keep these hobby-recognition cues visible: human actively using Robotics, subfield-specific hardware, output, or process, purposeful interaction.

The scene must include: a concrete Robotics interaction.

Do not depict any of the following: generic coder at desk, glowing brain or meaningless holograms, readable code, logos, or brand names, front-facing monitor, laptop, tablet, or phone screen, screen used as the main recognition cue, screen full of code, terminal windows, editing timeline, waveform UI, or dashboard, readable UI labels, menus, controls, icons, charts, or spreadsheets, dense dashboard or multi-panel interface, glowing brain cliché, anonymous cyberpunk screen soup.

Also avoid these global failure modes: text, logos, watermarks, card borders, rarity labels, UI elements, floating unrelated objects, duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested, flat procedural vector art, bland corporate illustration, generic stock-photo composition, muddy focal hierarchy, overabstract imagery, generic concept wallpaper, confusing mixtures of different hobbies, pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image, readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks, recognisable copyrighted film/game/cartoon characters or franchise costumes, collage, split-screen, comic-panel, or multi-panel layouts, photoreal stock-photo rendering unless explicitly requested by the hobby recipe, the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image, title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy, poster, advertisement, magazine-cover, card-face, or editorial-page layout, text boxes, caption bands, lower-thirds, or deliberate blank space reserved for typography.
negative_constraints: readable code, logos, or brand names
front-facing monitor, laptop, tablet, or phone screen
screen used as the main recognition cue
editing timeline, waveform UI, or dashboard
readable UI labels, menus, controls, icons, charts, or spreadsheets
duplicated key objects unless explicitly requested
pseudo-text or gibberish lettering anywhere in the image
readable real-world brand names, logos, or trademarks
recognisable copyrighted film/game/cartoon characters or franchise costumes
collage, split-screen, comic-panel, or multi-panel layouts
photoreal stock-photo rendering unless explicitly requested by the hobby recipe
the hobby or interest name rendered anywhere in the image
title, subtitle, caption, heading, label, footer, explanatory copy, poster copy, or body copy
poster, advertisement, magazine-cover, card-face, or editorial-page layout
text boxes, caption bands, lower-thirds, or deliberate blank space reserved for typography
